newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Ekeus to brief U.N. Council before going to Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Ekeus to brief U.N. Council before going to Iraq.

text.p: Rolf Ekeus, head of U.N. Special Commission in charge of Iraqi disarmament, will brief the Security Council on Thursday, according to U.N. spokeswoman Sylvana Foa.

He will be explaining his latest report on Iraq's weapons of mass destruction before he leaves for Baghdad on Thursday evening for his periodic meetings with Tareq Aziz, Iraq's deputy prime minister. He expects to arrive in Baghdad on Saturday, his office said.

In his report, released last Friday, Ekeus said Baghdad had systematically concealed banned weapons. He particularly criticized Iraq's six purported final declarations on biological weapons saying that "major sections are incomplete, inaccurate or unsubstantiated."

A clean bill of health by the commission is a key requirement by the U.N. Security Council before the embargo on Iraqi oil exports can be lifted entirely. Iraq has been under sanctions since its invasion of Kuwait in August 1990.
